svg.aria-label: Diagram: Google Cloud naming rules compared across four services, the character-set conflict between Compute Engine and BigQuery, the fields safe to encode in an immutable name versus those belonging in labels or tags, and what must never appear in a name
svg.title: Resource naming on Google Cloud: what each service allows, what a name should encode, and what will not survive three years
svg.text: A name is the only metadata with no update path
So it gets only the fields that need none. Everything else belongs somewhere it can be corrected on a Tuesday.
Four services, four sets of rules — read this as four products, not one platform
Project ID
6–30 chars. Lowercase, numbers, hyphens. Permanent, and globally unique forever.
Compute Engine
1–63 chars, RFC 1035. Hyphens yes, underscores no.
Storage bucket
3–63 chars. One global namespace shared by every user. Cannot be renamed.
BigQuery dataset
Up to 1,024 chars. Underscores yes, hyphens no. Case-sensitive by default.
The two separators everyone reaches for are each banned somewhere. No literal template is legal everywhere.
Safe in a name — still true at deletion
Resource type. A bucket never becomes a subnet,
which is why the blueprint leads with the prefix.
Region or zone, where the resource is bound to one.
Workload, cautiously — use the internal codename,
not the product name that marketing owns.
A random suffix, so provisioning never fails on a
name a stranger already claimed.
prj-c-logging-a1b2 — type, env, description, suffix.
Belongs in a label or tag — it will change
Owning team. Reorganisations outpace the lifetime
of the resources. The most common naming regret.
Cost centre. Renumbered by finance on their own
schedule, with no reference to your estate.
Ticket or change reference. Meaningful for weeks,
encoded in a name for years.
Environment, for anything policy must enforce on —
a name cannot be read by a policy engine.
Up to 64 labels per resource, editable at any time.
Never in a name: the bucket namespace is a public surface
Bucket names are publicly visible, and anyone can probe for the existence of a bucket. Google says directly: no user IDs,
no email addresses, no project names or numbers, no personally identifiable information. Cloud SQL says the same.
A convention encoding the customer or the internal code makes your estate enumerable by guessing.
Spend the 30-character budget on purpose, before choosing fields
Type prefix and separator 4 — environment code and separator 2 — random suffix and separator 5.
Eleven characters of overhead before a single descriptive word, leaving nineteen that mean something.
The permanence test, applied to every field before it enters a name:
Will this still be true when the resource is deleted? Not true today, and not unlikely to change — still true at the end.
Generate names from a module rather than a wiki page: a documented convention is followed only while the page is read.
A name is not documentation. It is an address, and an address only has to keep pointing at the same place.
